raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On SM100, `fused_q` now writes the DSA indexer weights directly in BF16, the dtype DeepGEMM's MQA logits kernels
take. This removes the FP32 to BF16 copy `mqa_logits_mx_inputs` launched on every indexer call.

## Claims

- One fewer kernel per indexer call (prefill chunks and decode) on SM100/SM103 for DSA models using `fused_q`
  (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x). The logits are bit-identical: the weights are still computed in FP32 and rounded to
  BF16 once, just inside `fused_q` instead of in a separate copy.
- Other platforms are unchanged (FP32 weights).
- On InferenceX AgentX, GLM-5.3 vs SGLang: together with #62171 and #62172, decode time on the same turns drops 2.0-2.9% on 4x GB200 (2.5-4.1% on 4x B300) at concurrency 1-16; by the forward benchmark this PR is about 1/6 of that.

## Validation

- `tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v32_norm_rope.py` on B300 (SM103): 214 passed, 8 skipped. The weight
  assertions now check BF16 output on SM100 and FP32 elsewhere.
- Target verify forward latency (`vllm bench forward`, GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4, dummy weights, exact KV lengths, MTP verify shapes of B requests x 4 tokens, `max_model_len` 1M, CUDA graph; spread < 0.1%), B300:

  | shape | before (us) | after (us) |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1x4 @25K | 8724.8 | 8696.4 (-0.33%) |
  | 3x4 @25K | 12264.2 | 12231.4 (-0.27%) |
  | 7x4 @25K | 17688.4 | 17649.7 (-0.22%) |
  | 1x4 @94K | 8829.5 | 8799.6 (-0.34%) |
  | 3x4 @94K | 12561.0 | 12532.0 (-0.23%) |
  | 7x4 @94K | 18148.9 | 18116.0 (-0.18%) |

- Exactness: with real MTP verification (32 GSM8K questions, greedy, one at a time), this PR stacked with the other GLM-5 top-k changes gives the same outputs (32/32) and the same acceptance length (3.4904) as main.
- End to end on B300 x4 (SM103): GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4, MTP 3 with synthetic acceptance length 3.0 (fixed step count), `max_model_len` 1M, FP8 KV, CUDA graphs (default sizes). Decode ms/token per request, median of 9 repetitions of (T1200 - T200) / 1000 on cached prompts (repetition spread at B=1 is about 1.5%):

  | context | B | main | this PR |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 25K | 1 | 3.182 | 3.171 (-0.3%) |
  | 94K | 1 | 3.227 | 3.207 (-0.6%) |

  Batches of 3-7 move within the measurement noise (about ±1.5%).

<details>
<summary>InferenceX AgentX setup and full results (GLM-5.3-NVFP4, vLLM vs SGLang)</summary>

InferenceX c801c9f2d AgentX scenario (pinned AIPerf), 20-minute fast mode, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 rev e3b8f9f2, TP4, MTP 3
(synthetic acceptance 2.99), native KV offload 135 GB per rank, Rust frontend, MoE autotune, `max-num-seqs` =
2 x concurrency. vLLM is main dcd07967ca with its default linear backend and default CUDA graph config, plus the
PRs cumulatively. SGLang a916d91cd3 with IMEX, TRT-LLM all-reduce fusion, `--mem-fraction-static 0.90`. Fresh
server per point, SGLang and the four vLLM variants alternating per concurrency. "Decode" is request latency minus
TTFT, summed over the turns both runs finished (a few hundred per point); fast-mode throughput alone moves about
+-2% between runs.

4x GB200 (c=1/4 on driver 580.173.02; c=8/16 on 580.178.04 after a host reinstall, SGLang rerun there too):

| decode time vs SGLang, same turns | main | + #62170, #62171, #62172 | + #62174 (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6630, flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6631, flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6632) | + #62173 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| c=1 | +8.9% | +5.8% | +4.0% | +3.2% |
| c=4 | +12.7% | +10.6% | +7.3% | +7.3% |
| c=8 | +12.3% | +9.5% | +7.9% | +7.3% |
| c=16 | -22.6% | -25.0% | -24.5% | -24.3% |

| tok/s/GPU vs SGLang | main | + #62170, #62171, #62172 | + #62174 | + #62173 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| c=1 (SGLang 5,681) | -3.2% | -0.4% | -1.1% | +0.6% |
| c=4 (SGLang 6,783) | -0.6% | -2.4% | +0.4% | -1.7% |
| c=8 (SGLang 11,799) | -11.5% | -9.4% | -8.8% | -8.4% |
| c=16 (SGLang 10,529) | +44.7% | +45.6% | +45.8% | +46.8% |

| decode time vs the previous column, same turns | + #62170, #62171, #62172 | + #62174 | + #62173 |
|---|---|---|---|
| GB200 c=1 / c=4 / c=8 / c=16 | -2.9% / -2.0% / -2.1% / -2.9% | -1.6% / -3.1% / -1.2% / -0.4% | -0.8% / -0.9% / -0.5% / -0.1% |
| B300 c=1 / c=4 | -2.5% / -4.1% | -1.6% / -3.1% | -0.5% / -1.1% |

#62170, #62171 and #62172 were measured together; `vllm bench forward` (target verify forward, spread < 0.1%)
splits their gain about 1/6, 1/2 and 1/3.

</details>

## Details

`mqa_logits_use_mx_scales()` already decides that the SM100 logits kernels take BF16 weights, and
`mqa_logits_mx_inputs` returned `weights.to(torch.bfloat16)`. That was a real copy kernel for every indexer call,
since `fused_q` (Triton and CuTeDSL) always wrote FP32. `fused_q` now allocates its weights output in the dtype the
logits kernels take, and both kernels cast on store. `.to(torch.bfloat16)` then returns the tensor as-is.

The CuTeDSL kernel's compile key gains the output dtype.

---

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>
